## Quarto

Quarto enables you to weave together content and executable code into a finished document. To learn more about Quarto see <https://quarto.org>.

## Running Code

When you click the **Render** button a document will be generated that includes both content and the output of embedded code. You can embed code like this:

```{r}
1 + 1
```

You can add options to executable code like this

```{r}
#| echo: false
2 * 2
```

The `echo: false` option disables the printing of code (only output is displaye

### 1.4 run the linear regression by group

## 

```{r}


library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

# Keep only ID1 and ID2
data_clean <- data %>%
  filter(ID %in% c("ID1", "ID2")) %>%
  droplevels()

# Verify the cleaned data
table(data_clean$ID)
table(data_clean$GROUP, data_clean$ID)

# Check the number of rows
nrow(data_clean)
```

```{r}

summary_data <- data_clean %>%
  group_by(GROUP, ID) %>%
  summarise(
    n = sum(!is.na(MovementTime)),
    mean_MT = mean(MovementTime, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_MT = sd(MovementTime, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

print(summary_data)
```

```{r}
models <- data_clean %>%
  group_by(GROUP) %>%
  group_modify(~ {
    fit <- lm(MovementTime ~ ID_numeric, data = .x)
    
    tibble(
      intercept = unname(coef(fit)[1]),
      slope = unname(coef(fit)[2]),
      equation = sprintf(
        "MT = %.3f + %.3f * ID",
        coef(fit)[1], coef(fit)[2]
      )
    )
  }) %>%
  ungroup()

print(models)
```

## 1.5 Save a graph in a PDF file for publication

```{r}


library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

# 1. Calculate group means and standard deviations
summary_data <- data_clean %>%
  group_by(GROUP, ID_numeric) %>%
  summarise(
    MeanMT = mean(MovementTime, na.rm = TRUE),
    SD = sd(MovementTime, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# 2. Fit a separate regression for each group
models <- data_clean %>%
  group_by(GROUP) %>%
  group_modify(~ {
    fit <- lm(MovementTime ~ ID_numeric, data = .x)
    
    tibble(
      intercept = unname(coef(fit)[1]),
      slope = unname(coef(fit)[2])
    )
  }) %>%
  ungroup()

# 3. Generate regression lines across the graph
prediction_data <- models %>%
  group_by(GROUP) %>%
  group_modify(~ {
    x <- seq(-0.3, 6.3, length.out = 200)
    
    tibble(
      ID_numeric = x,
      PredictedMT = .x$intercept[1] +
        .x$slope[1] * x
    )
  }) %>%
  ungroup()

# 4. Prepare clearly separated equation labels
equations <- models %>%
  mutate(
    label = sprintf(
      "MT = %.3f + %.3f * ID",
      intercept, slope
    ),
    x = 0.5,
    y = case_when(
      GROUP == "pp" ~ 5.45,
      GROUP == "ap" ~ 5.10,
      GROUP == "cp" ~ 4.75
    )
  )

# 5. Match the reference colors
group_colors <- c(
  "pp" = "red",
  "ap" = "green3",
  "cp" = "blue"
)

# 6. Create the publication-style graph
p <- ggplot() +
  
  # Dashed regression lines
  geom_line(
    data = prediction_data,
    aes(
      x = ID_numeric,
      y = PredictedMT,
      color = GROUP,
      group = GROUP
    ),
    linetype = "dashed",
    linewidth = 0.55
  ) +
  
  # Mean +/- standard deviation
  geom_errorbar(
    data = summary_data,
    aes(
      x = ID_numeric,
      ymin = MeanMT - SD,
      ymax = MeanMT + SD,
      color = GROUP
    ),
    width = 0.08,
    linewidth = 0.55
  ) +
  
  # Mean points
  geom_point(
    data = summary_data,
    aes(
      x = ID_numeric,
      y = MeanMT,
      color = GROUP
    ),
    shape = 1,
    size = 3
  ) +
  
  # Solid lines joining observed means
  geom_line(
    data = summary_data,
    aes(
      x = ID_numeric,
      y = MeanMT,
      color = GROUP,
      group = GROUP
    ),
    linewidth = 0.7
  ) +
  
  # Non-overlapping equations
  geom_text(
    data = equations,
    aes(
      x = x,
      y = y,
      label = label,
      color = GROUP
    ),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    hjust = 0,
    vjust = 0.5,
    size = 3.6
  ) +
  
  scale_color_manual(
    values = group_colors,
    breaks = c("pp", "ap", "cp"),
    name = "GROUP"
  ) +
  
  # Numeric ID axis
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = 0:6,
    expand = expansion(mult = 0),
    limits = c(-0.3, 6.3)
  ) +
  
  # Movement time in seconds
  scale_y_continuous(
    breaks = -1:6,
    expand = expansion(mult = 0)
  ) +
  
  coord_cartesian(
    ylim = c(-1.3, 6.7)
  ) +
  
  labs(
    x = "ID",
    y = "Mean Movement Time (s)"
  ) +
  
  theme_classic(base_size = 12) +
  
  theme(
    axis.title = element_text(size = 12),
    axis.text = element_text(size = 10, color = "black"),
    axis.line = element_line(linewidth = 0.5),
    axis.ticks = element_line(linewidth = 0.5),
    legend.position = "right",
    legend.title = element_text(size = 11),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 10),
    plot.margin = margin(10, 15, 10, 10)
  )

# Display
print(p)


```

## save as pdf

```{r}
ggsave(
  filename = "MovementTime_Regression.pdf",
  plot = p,
  width = 8,
  height = 6,
  units = "in",
  device = "pdf"
)
```
